title: Infrared Memory of a Majorana Shutter
summary: We study a finite-width Majorana shutter as a local, time-dependent scattering defect and determine which features of its infrared memory are insensitive to the microscopic spatial profile. For a smooth shutter, the zero-frequency scattering matrix is fixed by the integrated coupling, while finite-width corrections vanish in the long-wavelength limit. A time-dependent switch then produces an infrared Bogoliubov kernel whose singular part is controlled by the change in this scattering matrix.
